body parts/elbow: "is famously impossible for a person to lick": true for almost everyone, but a few very flexible people can manage it
body parts/kidney: "is about the size of a closed fist": the usual textbook comparison; an adult kidney is about 10 to 12 cm long, so it is approximate
body parts/liver: "weighs about one and a half kilograms in an adult": typical adult range is roughly 1.2 to 1.6 kg, so 'about' carries the claim
body parts/skull: "is made of plates that slowly fuse together as a child grows": the soft spots close by about age two, but some sutures only fully fuse in adulthood; the clause simplifies
body parts/stomach: "is pumped out after someone swallows poison": widely known, but gastric lavage is now rarely used in modern emergency care
body parts/thumb: "has two segments where each of its neighbours has three": counts the phalanges; all digits also have a metacarpal in the palm
"is called green in someone with a gift for gardening": 'green thumb' is the American idiom; British English says 'green fingers', which a reader may take as pointing to the other concept
body parts/toe: "is where painful gout most often strikes for the first time": true of the base joint of the big toe specifically, not of every toe
